title: perf(objectql): recompute roll-up summaries with one grouped aggregate per field and one write per parent
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
Part of #33795
Clause-②: no (same values for every summary kind on both dialects; fewer statements; no accepted shape or public export widens; if collapsing a parent's per-field updates fires a parent hook fewer times, the PR body says so, as the card asks; the dev confirms)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:子记录写入后重算父记录汇总字段时,每个父记录只写一次(带上全部汇总字段),多行写入时每个汇总字段只做一次分组聚合,不再按父记录逐个聚合。
- 为什么改:原来每个汇总字段、每个父记录都要聚合一次再更新一次。50 行批量插入、2 个汇总字段要 81 条 SQL,现在 33 条;逐行更新 50 行从 550 条降到 400 条。SQLite 与 PostgreSQL 16 实测,数值完全一致。
- 风险与回滚:父记录的更新钩子、校验、审计、实时事件次数变少(两个汇总字段时从每次重算两次变为一次,一次带两个字段)。回滚即还原 `engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` 与 `summary-aggregate.ts` 两个文件。
- 先看:`packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` 的 `recomputeSummaries`(两阶段与自引用回退分支);`packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts` 的 `aggregateSummaryValues`;`packages/qa/dogfood/test/rollup-grouped-recompute-33795.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/rollup-grouped-recompute-33795.test.ts`,预期 SQLite 两条测试通过,并打印 `createMany {0:1, 1:32, 2:33}`、`updateLoop {0:150, 1:350, 2:400}`。
- 需要你做的:卡片的另一半(bulk updateMany 把逐行重算推迟到批末)需要你在决策卡上选方案:它要改 `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 并给引擎契约新增一个成员,超出本单认领范围。

## What changes

`recomputeSummaries` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts`) now works in two steps.

1. It collects, for every summary descriptor over the child, the parent ids the write touched. Then it computes each descriptor's value for all of those parents. With one parent, it asks the existing one-parent aggregate (`aggregateSummaryValue`), so the query a single-row write runs is unchanged. With several parents, it asks a new grouped aggregate, `aggregateSummaryValues` in `summary-aggregate.ts`: `where fk in (…) group by fk`, at most 500 ids per statement (`SUMMARY_GROUPED_AGGREGATE_CHUNK`). The descriptor's filter is ANDed in, as before. A parent with no matching row gets `summaryEmptySetValue`, as before.
2. It writes each parent once, through the engine `update`, carrying all of its summary fields, with the same elevated context and the same `SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_WRITE` marker.

A roll-up graph that leads from a parent back to the child object (a roll-up over its own object, or a cycle across objects) keeps per-parent order. Each parent's aggregates are read just before its write, because there an earlier parent's write can move a later parent's child rows. That parent is still written once with all its fields.

Failures keep their shape. A failed aggregate records one failure per parent for that field. A failed parent write records one failure per field it carried, and the other parents are still written. The transient retry wraps each aggregate and each write.

The ADR-0144 D6 roll-up channel (`ROLLUP_AGGREGATE_OPTION`) rides the grouped aggregate too. Every group is one parent's rows through the master_detail, so a child amount that follows its parent's currency is one currency per group. It rides only when every id in the chunk is a concrete id, as on the one-parent aggregate.

### What a parent's write path sees now (the card asks this to be said)

The parent's update path (hooks, validation, audit, realtime) still runs for every parent the write touched. It runs fewer times. A parent with N summary fields over one child was updated N times per recompute, one field per payload. It is now updated once, with all N fields in one payload. So `beforeUpdate` / `afterUpdate` hooks on the parent fire once instead of N times, the audit trail gets one entry instead of N, and realtime publishes one event instead of N. A validation rule on the parent judges the final state of all its summary fields together, never a state where one field is fresh and another stale. A summary over a summary still recomputes up the chain, because each parent write is an engine `update` with its own recompute. The grandparent is now recomputed once per parent write instead of once per field.

### What this PR does not do: the `updateMany` deferral

The card's Target also asks the bulk `updateMany` to defer the recompute from per row to the end of the batch. That loop is not in `@objectstack/objectql`. It is `runUpdateManyLoop` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts`, which calls `engine.update` once per row and reaches the engine only through `MetadataHostEngine` / `IDataEngine`. The engine cannot tell those calls are one batch. Deferring needs a batch scope that the protocol opens and the engine honours. That is a new member on the engine contract the protocol is typed against, plus a change in `metadata-protocol`. Both are outside the claimed file surface, and the first is an accepted-shape change, so it went back to the seat as a decision. The card stays open (`Part of`, not `Fixes`).

Through `updateMany`, this PR already collapses the per-row cost from 4 statements per field to 1 per field plus 3, and that is all it changes there.

## Tests

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/rollup-grouped-recompute-33795.test.ts` (new) runs the real engine over a real `SqlDriver`. It counts statements with knex's `query` event. Cells: SQLite (better-sqlite3) always, and PostgreSQL when `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set.
  - Statement pins: a 50-row `createMany` over 10 parents, and a loop of 50 engine `update`s (the per-row writes the bulk door issues), with 0, 1 and 2 summary fields.
  - Value parity across count, sum, min, max, avg, filtered count and filtered sum. It checks after inserts, a re-parent, an update loop, a predicate update and a predicate delete. Every stored value must equal the one-parent `aggregateSummaryValue` and a hand count.
- `packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts`, a new top-level `describe` in the shared harness: one parent write and one hook run per parent with both fields; one aggregate per field per batch; a single-row write still asks the one-parent equality; a summary over a summary; a self-referencing roll-up takes the per-parent path with no `$in`; a failed parent write reports one failure per field it carried.
- Three existing doubles learn a field's `$in`: `engine-summary-recompute-context.test.ts`, `engine-summary-retry.test.ts` and `engine-update-prior-read-scope.test.ts`. A re-parent now names two parents in one grouped aggregate, and those fakes threw on, or ignored, the operator every real driver serves. No assertion changed.

| statements (engine, admin/system) | 0 summaries | 1 | 2 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `createMany` 50 rows, 10 parents, before | 1 | 41 | 81 |
| `createMany` 50 rows, 10 parents, after | 1 | 32 | 33 |
| 50 single-row `update`s, before | 150 | 350 | 550 |
| 50 single-row `update`s, after | 150 | 350 | 400 |

Identical on SQLite and PostgreSQL 16, at both commits.

## Acceptance notes

- PostgreSQL in CI: no CI job that runs `@objectstack/dogfood` provisions `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, so the PostgreSQL cell is a named skip there. It was run locally against a private PostgreSQL 16.15 (readings below). The SQLite cell runs in the dogfood shards.
- The card's figures (209/249/289 and 358/558/758) are REST readings with permission reads included. The table above is engine-level, so the absolute numbers differ and the per-field deltas match the card's measurement: +40 per field before, and +31 for the first field with +1 for each further field after.

## Verification

<details><summary>Red first: the pins on the base engine (80cdbd4e0f)</summary>

The two engine files were restored from the base, objectql rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight` confirmed `aggregateSummaryValues` was absent from `dist/`.

```
AssertionError: {"createMany":{"0":1,"1":41,"2":81},"updateLoop":{"0":150,"1":350,"2":550}}: expected 40 to be 31
Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)      -- both statement pins red (SQLite, PostgreSQL); both value-parity tests green
```

Unit pins on base source: `writes each parent once ...` and `a single-row write ... writes the parent once` were red (2 failed, 27 passed). The chain, self-reference and failure-report pins were green, because they pin preserved behaviour. The restore was proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty porcelain.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations, each through ablation-replace.mjs and rebuilt, marker proven in dist/</summary>

- Grouping ablated (each descriptor aggregates per parent, collapsed writes kept): `{"createMany":{"0":1,"1":41,"2":51},"updateLoop":{"0":150,"1":350,"2":400}}`. The statement pins went red (2 failed), and value parity stayed green.
- Collapse ablated (one parent write per field, grouping kept): `{"createMany":{"0":1,"1":32,"2":63},"updateLoop":{"0":150,"1":350,"2":550}}`. The statement pins went red (2 failed), and value parity stayed green.
- Restore: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, both markers absent from the rebuilt `dist/`, and the suite green again (4 passed).
</details>

<details><summary>Local runs at 02e274bd70</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 603 files. The first run had 3 failed, all the `$in`-less doubles above. After the double fix, those 3 files plus `summary-rollup.test.ts` give 61/61 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/rollup-grouped-recompute-33795.test.ts` with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`: 4/4 passed. `statements sqlite` and `statements postgresql` were both `{"createMany":{"0":1,"1":32,"2":33},"updateLoop":{"0":150,"1":350,"2":400}}`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0, and `check:test-typecheck` held.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 71 derived. 70 ran with exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (the whole repo is not built here), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI. `--ran` reconciled: 70 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` 27c0b206eb: clean. No open PR touches these files.
</details>

## Fix round 1

Answers L1 ACCEPT 6923522845 (thread L1-a). Head `1789606ebf`, one commit on top of `02e274bd70`. No behaviour change, no changeset change.

- **S1 (pinned).** `record-currency-guards.test.ts` gains `[#33795] a batch of lines across two parents totals each in one grouped aggregate, as one line at a time does`. One `insert` of four `pp_line` rows across `inv_usd` (USD) and `inv_eur` (EUR) asks exactly one `pp_line` read carrying `invoice $in [inv_usd, inv_eur]` (the grouped `aggregateSummaryValues`), records no recompute failure, and lands subtotals 150 and 100, equal to a second engine fed the same lines one at a time (the one-parent `aggregateSummaryValue`). The same grouped statement asked through `engine.aggregate` without the roll-up channel is still refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400: the grouping does not make it one currency, the channel does.
- **Green on first run, so ablated.** Mutation: the grouped path's channel `concrete ? { [ROLLUP_AGGREGATE_OPTION]: desc.fkField } : undefined` replaced by `undefined` in `summary-aggregate.ts`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The pin went red with `SummaryRecomputeError: Roll-up summary recompute failed after retries for 2 parent record(s)`, the exact failure S1 named. Restored: blob back to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **N1 (fixed).** The `ROLLUP_AGGREGATE_OPTION` docblock and the module header in `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` now name `aggregateSummaryValues` (grouped by the same `fkField`, one parent per group) as the second setter. Comment only.
- **N2 (no code change).** The wider read-to-write window under concurrent child writes is judged in the contract-review record on this PR; behaviour unchanged.

<details><summary>Verification on 1789606ebf</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` under the verify lock: Test Files 603 passed (603), Tests 13476 passed (13476); `check:test-typecheck` OK.
- Targeted gates: 18 of the 74 the branch derives (those reading this round's two files), each exit 0; the other 56 are CI's.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree`: clean against `origin/main` `c9ef6538bf` and against `claude/issue-33795-batch-deferral` `7480459d6c`.

</details>
